To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the histone tails participate in the anchoring of the incoming viral DNA in chromatin, thus facilitating its integration into the host genome.
HIV-1 integrases interact with the amino-terminal tails of nucleosomal histone H4 and that these interactions are important for the integration of viral DNA into chromatin.
the amino-terminal tails of histones H3 and H4 interact with HIV-1 IN, and that these interactions modulate the association between the intesome and the nucleosomal core particle.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms that underlie the interaction of HIV-1 IN with the nucleosome and its functional consequences.
the functional association of the HIV-1 IN with histone tails.
the molecular mechanisms that govern the integration of the retrovirus DNA genome into host cell chromatin and how the host response affects the outcome of the integration process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the histone amino-terminal tail is a critical factor in the integration process of the HIV-1 proviral DNA.
HIV-1 IN interacts with histones and this is important for integration.
the amino-terminal histone tails are important for the nucleosome binding of the HIV-1 IN, which is a key step in the retroviral integration process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the amino-terminal tail from histone H4 is required for optimal nucleosomal integration and that it interacts directly with the carboxy-terminus of IN.

the amino-terminal tails of histone H4 and histone H2A may be involved in the functional association between HIV intasome and nucleosome for integration into chromatin, and this association is required for efficient integration.
the histone tails play a role in modulating the functional association between IN and the nucleosome.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the nucleosome is not an inert substrate for HIV-1 integration.
histone amino-terminal tail sequences can be used to modulate HIV-1 integration in the host cell.
the intasome is a dynamic entity whose interactions with chromatin are regulated and modulated during integration.
